title: Domestication of the dog
summary: The dog was the first domesticated animal, but when domestication began, and whether it happened once or several times, remains uncertain. Domestic dogs were in western Europe and the Near East by at least 14,000 BC. The earliest known dog burial, about 14,000 years old, comes from Bonn-Oberkassel in Germany. Claims for dogs before the Last Glacial Maximum are disputed.

uncertainty.note: Archaeological consensus dates the earliest undisputed morphological dog remains to roughly 15,000–14,000 BP (with burials such as Bonn-Oberkassel at c. 14,000 BP / 14,000 cal BC), while genetic divergence models span 20,000–40,000 years ago.
